    • The negotiations did, however, yield an agreement for further discussions to develop new rules by 2028.
    • Delegates from 128 states that are parties to the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) had been meeting in Geneva since Monday amid rising concerns over the use of the so-called killer robots in global conflicts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    United Nations talks on regulating lethal autonomous weapons systems ended on Saturday without an agreement on a legally binding ban.

    The negotiations did, however, yield an agreement for further discussions to develop new rules by 2028.

    Delegates from 128 states that are parties to the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) had been meeting in Geneva since Monday amid rising concerns over the use of the so-called killer robots in global conflicts.

    The conference ended early on Saturday in what campaigners deemed a "weakened" outcome, following several hours of overnight parleying.

    Nearly 100 nations had called for negotiations on a legally binding agreement on the systems capable of killing without a human making the final decision to fire.

    UN Secretary-General António Guterres, Pope Leo XIV and the Red Cross had also supported a ban on killer robots.

    However, countries that have the technology, including arms-producing giants like the ​US, Russia ‌and Israel, were among those opposing the mandate.

    Ultimately, the 128 countries  "agreed to launch the elaboration of an international instrument on lethal autonomous weapons systems, which should be conducted over the next two years", the conference's Swiss chair, Julien Thoni, told the media on Saturday.

    But while Thoni hailed a multilateral diplomacy delivering "concrete results" even in "today's deeply divided world," rights groups expressed disappointment at the minimal agreement.

    "States adopted a watered-down mandate that fails to chart a clear path towards a legally binding instrument," news agency AFP quoted Stop Killer Robots, a global coalition of over 300 organizations, as saying.

    "Over 95 states expressed their support for a treaty. In the final hours, a small number of states weakened the mandate introducing uncertainty about the legal status of the final document," it added.

    The group had earlier noted that autonomous weapons systems were already reaching the battlefield and such systems had been tested or deployed, including in the Ukraine war.

    #70348. The pros and cons of using a dumb phone over a smartphone in 2026

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (606 w)

    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

    The pros and cons of using a dumb phone over a smartphone in 2026

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Dumb phones are cheap and distraction-free, but you'll probably miss your smartphone.
    • Smartphones have become the standard for mobile devices, even if you don't use many of the features they offer.
    • Sources indicate that but does that really make sense in today's world?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Dumb phones are cheap and distraction-free, but you'll probably miss your smartphone.

    Smartphones have become the standard for mobile devices, even if you don't use many of the features they offer. Still, there seems to be a demand for what are now called "dumb phones" — cheap, old-school-style phones that offer only basic features like calls and text messages. Some of them have a camera and can run apps, but they aren't really designed for that type of business. The idea here is to get rid of the distractions of modern smartphones.

    Sources indicate that but does that really make sense in today's world? Here's what you should know about these pared-down devices in order to make a smart decision about owning a dumb phone in 2026 and beyond.

    According to recent reports, for most people looking for a dumb phone, less screen time seems to be the biggest benefit. It can be hard to avoid social media, emails and constant notifications on a smartphone, even with features like the iPhone's Screen Time. For those who can't go a few minutes without checking their cell screen, simply setting a limit on apps usually doesn't help much. With a dumb phone, you can't even install most of those apps. Many dumb phones are limited to running built-in apps for making calls, sending messages and setting alarms. Others run a basic version of Android that lets you install some apps, including games, GPS navigation and music players, but compared with modern smartphones, they won't let you do much.

    It has been revealed that battery life is another plus here. With small screens and underpowered chips, these phones can last for days on a single charge. That's the case with the TCL Flip Go, a dumb phone with a battery rated to last around 14 days on standby. There simply isn't a regular smartphone capable of going that long without being plugged in, so these dumb phones can be great companions for specific adventures like road trips or hikes.

    According to recent reports, another thing people like about dumb phones is privacy — having a phone without third-party apps means fewer trackers collecting your data to sell to advertisers. These phones are also very cheap and usually cost less than $100 in the US, while the lowest-priced Android phones usually cost twice as much.

    The thing is, you probably shouldn't replace your regular smartphone with a dumb phone. Having one of these means you're giving up a lot of convenience, such as mobile wallets like Apple Pay or Samsung Pay, or having a good portable camera with you. Plus, if you go with a model that doesn't run any third-party apps, you won't be able to get an Uber or use Google Maps. Streaming apps like Spotify or Apple Music may also not be available on these phones.

    According to recent reports, messaging works, but you'll probably have to rely on SMS or RCS — there's no iMessage, and in many cases, not even WhatsApp or Telegram. Internet access also varies among these phones, with most of them limited to 4G networks. There are some that work on 5G networks, but these are harder to find and are also more expensive. You'll additionally sacrifice two-factor authentication apps like Google Authenticator, and banking apps probably won't work either.

    Sources indicate that there are good reasons to have a dumb phone, sure, especially if you've been feeling overwhelmed by notifications and algorithms. But in all practicality, it's best to think of it as a second option to the smartphone you already have, not as a full replacement.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Exclusive: Countries at Cop31 are being urged to commit to deriving 35% of their energy from electricity by 2035.

    • Industry observers note that wang Yi, a professor of energy and environment policy at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a senior adviser to China’s government, said: “End-use electrification is a very clear direction.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Exclusive: Countries at Cop31 are being urged to commit to deriving 35% of their energy from electricity by 2035.

    China is pushing for rapid electrification of its economy using low-carbon energy and will help other countries do the same, a senior member of the Chinese delegation at the Cop31 UN climate summit has mentioned.

    Industry observers note that wang Yi, a professor of energy and environment policy at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a senior adviser to China’s government, said: “End-use electrification is a very clear direction. We can follow this direction while making the source of electricity clean. That’s the way to go forward.”.

    China is the biggest emitter of greenhouse gases by far, producing more than a quarter of the world’s total, so its push for electrification is significant.

    But in the second draft text of the probable outcome from Cop31, released on Thursday, the electrification pledge was downgraded to one of a suite of voluntary options countries can take up to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions.

    Recent findings suggest that in an interview with the Guardian at the talks, Wang mentioned: “China will do our best to realise clean end-use electrification, and also help other countries to improve. China has significantly reduced the cost of clean technology and products and we would like to share our experience with other countries.”.

    Experts have noted electrification is the next vital step in the shift to a low-carbon economy, as the only way to diminish the close to 80% of fossil fuels still used for primary energy, mostly for transport, heating and industry.

    While civil society organisations want any commitment made on electrification to specify that it must be met from clean sources, a pledge that leaves the choice to countries is likely to have more widespread support, as many – including China and India – are resistant to anything they feel smacks of “top down” interference in national plans.

    But campaigners argue that allowing individual countries to decide risks leaving the door open to more gas-fired power plants. Some compromise language is also possible that would urge countries to decarbonise their power.

    Last year, electricity made up nearly 30% of China’s energy use and it is on track to make that 35% by 2030. Electricity is several times more efficient than fossil fuels, meaning that it takes far less energy to run electric vehicles, heat pumps and industrial processes than their fossil fuel counterparts.

    Wang mentioned China was happy with the 2035 target, but that it would be harder to meet if the electricity was required to come entirely from low-carbon sources. “For this target, no problem. But if you think about ensuring clean electrification, that may be a little bit difficult, even for China. For other countries, it’s even more difficult,” he said.

    China still has a large number of coal-fired power stations and is planning some new ones, though fewer than before. Wang mentioned this would be used for back-up during the transition to clean energy.

    It has been revealed that one of the key complications at Cop31 is the “transition away from fossil fuels”, which was one of the resolutions passed at the Cop28 summit in Dubai in 2023, but which countries have failed to flesh out since. The phrase was included in the first draft of the “cover decision” outcome from Cop31, presented on Monday, but excised from the second draftissued on Thursday, to the dismay of many countries and campaigners.

    Wang said: “We agree with paragraph 28 of the UAE consensus [the transition resolution]. But maybe different countries have different roadmaps. It’s very difficult to have only one unified roadmap for every country. So maybe we will help other countries to have their own country-based solutions, to realise their own national way of establishing a new renewable-based power system.”.

    In a recent development, china is also concerned about trade barriers to its clean technology exports, including the tariffs that the US under Donald Trump has placed on Chinese goods, and the “carbon border adjustment mechanism” (CBAM) imposed by the EU. The CBAM penalises imports from countries with looser regulations on carbon than the EU, which forces companies in high-carbon sectors to pay for their carbon emissions in order to level the playing field.

    In a recent development, some smaller developing countries have criticised the EU for its CBAM, warning that it will hamper their manufacturing industries. The EU said it had processes in place to ensure smaller developing countries were not hurt.

    Sources indicate that wang called for more work on trade complications at Cops. “They must come together to find a unified approach,” he said. “China and other developing countries, including the global south, disagree [with the EU] on this. But that’s why we should continue to strengthen our dialogue.”.

    Industry observers note that jiangwen Guo, a senior research fellow at the Chatham House thinktank, stated other countries could learn from China. “China has very consistent top-down policies [and] sets a clear direction with high consistency, then follows with learning by doing,” she said. “In the great energy transition, there is no one ahead of China. China is creating the model for the globe.”.

    It has been revealed that negotiators at Cop31, which was scheduled to end at 6pm on Friday, were sent home late on Friday after the talks stalled, with a latest draft text of a “cover decision” marking the main outcome of the negotiations not thought likely to emerge until some time on Saturday morning. The talks are likely to continue into Saturday and potentially beyond.

    According to recent reports, white House national cyber director Sean Cairncross will be stepping down from his role, Axios reported. The news comes as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress and as businesses across the country report a flurry of technical outages whose cause remains unknown.

    In a recent development, cairncross, the president’s principal adviser on national cybersecurity policy and strategy, took office in August 2025. Since then, he has met with top AI leaders and helped the Trump administration make key AI decisions, according to Axios. The outlet also reports that the split between Cairncross and the White House was amicable, and his departure was timed so that the White House could nab a Senate confirmation for his role before Democrats take control of Congress in January.

    Sources indicate that cairncross, a lawyer and longtime Republican operative, had no cybersecurity background when the Senate confirmed him 59–35. He previously served as the Republican National Committee’s chief operating officer and, during Trump’s first term, as CEO of the Millennium Challenge Corporation, a federal foreign aid agency. The office hasn’t been around long; Congress created it in early 2021, and Cairncross was only its third Senate-confirmed director. The first director, Chris Inglis, left after about 19 months, and the job then went about 10 months without a permanent director.

    We’ve reached out to the White House for comment.

    Karen Scarborough (left) and Anne Lindboe got to work with a two-handled saw.

    This year's Trafalgar Square Christmas tree has been cut down in a forest outside Oslo, ready to begin its journey to London.

    The 21m (69ft) tree, nicknamed Jolly Cheery, is about 75 years old. It was felled on Friday by the Lord Mayor of Westminster, Karen Scarborough, and the Mayor of Oslo, Anne Lindboe.

    Norway has sent a tree to the capital every year since 1947 as a thank you for Britain's support during World War Two, when King Haakon VII and the Norwegian government lived in exile in London.

    Its lights will be switched on by the two mayors at a ceremony in the square on Thursday, 3 December.

    Scarborough said: "It's my greatest honour to take part in this wonderful tradition for both the cities of Oslo and London.

    "This tree is a powerful symbol of friendship and peace, reminding us to be there for one another during the festive period.".

    The 21m tree has been nicknamed Jolly Cheery.

    Scarborough thanked "the people of Oslo and Norway for this truly fabulous gift" and added: "With the care and dedication of the team, I'm sure it will look magnificent on Trafalgar Square.".

    Lindboe noted: "Oslo has been sending a Christmas tree to London for almost eight decades, and every year we send a tree across the North Sea with the same message: we have not forgotten.

    "The tradition has a powerful history, and its message remains just as relevant today.

    "I hope Jolly Cheery spreads warmth and Christmas cheer to everyone who passes by, and reminds us how much it means to be there for one another, especially in difficult times.".

    Count the rings: Anne Lindboe (left) and Karen Scarborough (right) with a slice of the 75-year-old trunk.

    For the second year running, the tree was chosen with the help of a social media poll.

    Organisers stated it would travel by road in Norway and England using only electric and biodiesel vehicles, cutting the journey's carbon footprint by 80%. It will cross the North Sea on a regular cargo ship from the port of Brevik.

    Once in London, it will be decorated in the traditional Norwegian style, with 25m strings of festoon lighting fitted with energy-efficient bulbs.

    #70340. Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1303 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1303 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, in the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion.
    • According to recent reports, in a newly introduced Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025.
    • Some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, in the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion. The process, known as common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some of the tightest pairs of stars in the Universe form, but no one had ever caught it in the act.

    According to recent reports, in a newly introduced Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025. “It lasts for a few years, maybe a few decades,” Karambelkar remarked. “Stars evolve on time scales of millions of years. So, it’s really like a blip on the entire cosmic time scale.”.

    Some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk. Common envelope evolution is the leading explanation for that shrinkage. When one star in a binary grows old, it expands into a giant, and its outer layers can engulf its companion. The two then share a single, loosely bound envelope of gas. As the engulfed star drags through it, it loses orbital energy to friction and spirals inward. Depending on how much of the envelope gets lost, the pair either ends up in a much tighter orbit or merges.

    It has been revealed that karambelkar’s team spotted a candidate system where this might be happening while searching Andromeda for stars changing in brightness, using the Wide-field Infrared Transient Explorer (WINTER) telescope at Palomar Observatory and data from NASA’s Near-Earth Object Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (NEOWISE) mission. One giant had been brightening for seven years. “When a star first swallows its companion, it has a very subtle effect on its brightness,” Karambelkar remarked. “It slowly brightens, and a lot of light comes out in the infrared.”.

    In April 2025, Karambelkar’s team published a paper suggesting that this system, named AT 2025abao, was undergoing an engulfment in progress. Back then, though, they couldn’t rule out a competing explanation: a single star with instabilities deep within its core. So, they kept watching.

    The researchers reconstructed the history of the system using observations from about a dozen telescopes and surveys, going back to photographic sky plates from 1989. Until 2018, the star barely changed. Modeling those quiet years revealed a giant late in its life, about 350 times wider than the Sun. Its companion was impossible to see, however. “The giant star outshines the smaller star by a factor of about 18,000,” Karambelkar remarked.

    It has been revealed that to get around it, the team estimated the mass of the smaller companion based on the amount of dust the system had shed before the engulfment. The estimates suggested a star of roughly 0.7 solar masses.

    It has been revealed that between 2018 and early 2025, the giant brightened two- to threefold in visible light, swelling while its temperature stayed nearly constant. Karambelkar compares the process to a spacecraft reentering Earth’s atmosphere. The companion, skimming through the giant’s outer layers, was gradually seeing its orbit shrink, and the friction was heating up the envelope. The energy released by that drag matched the extra light the team observed.

    Industry observers note that then, the star’s visible light dropped by half while its infrared glow kept rising. NASA’s SPHEREx space telescope happened to catch it in July 2025, revealing that the giant had swollen to some 860 times the Sun’s width and wrapped itself in fresh dust.

    In October 2025, the star brightened roughly 100-fold in just 25 days, shining like 1.5 million Suns at its peak. “At one point, the rate at which the orbit was decaying became very, very fast,” Karambelkar said, comparing the release of the gravitational energy to an explosion. “The companion just fell very rapidly, very deep inside the envelope of the star, and it crashed into the core. That violent crash set off a bomb inside the star, and that explosion caused it to brighten very quickly and eject some of the material.”.

    It has been revealed that the eruption had all the hallmarks of a luminous red nova, a type of outburst known to come from merging stars—but an event the researchers weren’t expecting. “Honestly, our minds were blown,” Karambelkar stated. He said that this was evidence that this explosion was a consequence of the inspiraling of a binary companion. What made AT 2025abao special, though, was the giant itself.

    All previously known luminous red novae came from younger stars with dense, tightly bound outer layers, which inevitably drive both stars toward a merger. This one was an old giant with a loose, churning envelope—the setup that can also leave behind a surviving tight binary. To find out if the companion actually survived, the team looked at how AT 2025abao’s energy was spent.

    To predict how such events end, astronomers use a formula with an efficiency parameter describing how much of the energy lost by the sinking companion goes into blowing the envelope away. AT 2025abao highlighted that the energy goes to different places at different stages.

    Industry observers note that during the slow spiral, most of the energy escaped as light. In the final plunge, the companion released about a hundred times more energy, but only around 1 percent of it was radiated away. Nearly all the rest went into hurling a tenth of the envelope outward at about 10 times the speed needed to escape the giant’s gravity. The rest of the envelope stayed put, which suggests the companion merged with the giant’s core instead of surviving as a tight partner.

    Recent findings suggest that “Initially, when the rate of energy deposition is low, the star is able to puff up and adjust to this latest energy source inside it,” Karambelkar stated. “But once the energy deposition rate increases very promptly as the companion spirals even closer, the star can no longer adjust itself. At that point, it needs to throw out some of its material.”.

    The efficiency the team calculated fits values inferred from known post-engulfment binaries. But the formula assumes the energy is mostly spent expelling lots of the envelope. Here, most of it went into flinging a small amount of gas at high speeds. It turned out the formula works as a rule of thumb but misses some of the physics.

    In a recent development, in AT 2025abao, gas shed during the slow spiral piled up in the plane of the binary’s orbit, so the explosion’s ejecta could expand freely toward the poles even though it was blocked around the equator. That, Karambelkar argues, explains the hourglass-shaped nebulae seen around dying stars. “It had been an idea for a very long time that those hourglass shapes are shaped by binary interactions,” he noted. “It seems like what we’re seeing here confirms that hypothesis.”.

    The team admits it can’t yet be sure the stars merged, because dust formed from the ejected material hides whatever is left inside. “We want to continue monitoring the system for several years, possibly even decades, to watch the dust clear out and whatever is remaining inside emerge,” Karambelkar said. “That will conclusively tell us whether this merged or the binary system survived.” In the meantime, the team hopes to find many more such events involving stars of different masses and types.

    Telescopes we have today can detect them only as far as Andromeda, but the Vera Rubin Observatory and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope should spot them in about 100 Milky Way-like galaxies within some 50 million light-years. “We can have an influx of several of these events per year,” Karambelkar noted.

    Nature, 2026. DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-11221-z.

    Hegseth uses Venezuela visit to boast of Maduro’s capture by US military

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago.
    • Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.
    • Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago.

    Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.

    Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.

    Speaking outside the recently reopened US embassy in Venezuela’s capital, Caracas, on Wednesday, Hegseth said: “It’s a great honor to be here as the first United States secretary of war this century to set foot in Venezuela.​ Just one year ago my presence here … would have been deemed impossible, almost unimaginable.

    “In fact, exactly one year ago today … [Maduro] stood on a stage not too far from here and yelled mockingly, ‘Come and get me!’” Hegseth recalled, before adding sarcastically: “Well, we answered that call.

    “The reality is that … January 3 is the day that will go down in history as a day of liberation for Venezuela,” Hegseth claimed, although Maduro’s allies continue to hold power with US support.

    Earlier in the day, Hegseth was welcomed to the Miraflores Palace by Maduro’s former vice-president, Delcy Rodríguez, who became acting president with Donald Trump’s blessing after his abduction.

    It has been revealed that in the aftermath of the deadly US attack, Hegseth was one of the bluntest Trump administration voices when it came to celebrating the invasion. “Maduro had his chance … he effed around and he found out,” the defense secretary bragged.

    Speaking at the palace, Hegseth struck a more conciliatory tone as he vowed to deepen cooperation with Venezuela’s new leaders in brief comments that were broadcast by the state broadcaster VTV.

    “I stand here on behalf of President Trump, who sends his greeting and looks forward to the opportunities, not just militarily … but also economically: the incredible resource capabilities that your country has, that we look forward to unlocking together with you,” Hegseth told Rodríguez and senior cabinet members, including the defense and foreign ministers, Gustavo González López and Oliver Blanco.

    Recent findings suggest that hegseth said his visit to Rodríguez’s “beautiful country” was designed to re-establish and increase “defense cooperation” between “two great militaries” that less than a year ago were briefly at war. Earlier this month, the Latest York Times reported that Trump officials were trying to negotiate a long-term US troop presence in Venezuela as part of their push for regional hegemony.

    “I appreciate your leadership and commitment to your country,” Hegseth told Maduro’s successor, a once outspoken anti-imperialist leftist who has overseen an unlikely realignment with Washington since her ally was grabbed.

    During her five-minute address, Rodríguez, whose oil-rich country is widely seen to have become a US protectorate after January’s invasion, made no mention of Maduro, who is behind bars in Latest York City.

    But referring indirectly to his capture and the subsequent reconciliation with Washington, she told Hegseth: “Thanks to the political and geopolitical maturity of our governments, we have – in a very short period of time, just a few months – turned what were very difficult and very tough times for our people, into an extraordinary space for cooperation and mutual benefit.”.

    Rodríguez hailed the “historic” energy deal her government recently struck with Trump, who has called it “the biggest oil deal in world history” as well as “the spoils” of his “conquest” of Venezuela.

    Hegseth claimed the agreement, which reportedly involves 65bn barrels of reserves, “makes the strait of Hormuz a non-factor for the western hemisphere”.

    Critics of Rodríguez’s political movement painted Hegseth’s visit as a humiliating act of genuflection for a president with no choice but to roll out the red carpet for the man whose troops captured her boss.

    Writing on X, Luz Mely Reyes, a prominent Venezuelan journalist, said Hegseth’s visit was designed to underscore Washington’s “direct administration” of her country.

    “Ten months after Nicolás Maduro’s capture, Washington no longer needs to fire shots to remind everyone who is in charge: the mere presence on Venezuelan soil of the architect of the January incursion reaffirms that the country’s operational sovereignty is subject to the White House’s directives,” Reyes mentioned.

    Sources indicate that reyes suspected the visit also carried a message for members of Venezuela’s armed forces. “Domestically, the trip forces the military high command to legitimize the man who directed the extraction of their former commander in chief,” she said. “In this regard, I wonder whether it might be a message of discipline intended to prevent any pockets of resistance in the barracks.”.

    In a recent development, trump’s attempts to expand his Shield of the Americas anti-cartel coalition of Latin American governments suffered a major blow last month with the defeat of his far-right ally, Flávio Bolsonaro, in Brazil’s presidential election. The leftwing winner, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has indicated his country will not join the initiative.

    But Venezuela’s interim government is in little position to resist. During his surprise visit to Venezuela, Hegseth noted Venezuela had gone from being “our most aggressive regional threat to [being] a compliant security partner”. He praised Rodríguez for working “closely, pragmatically, and diligently with the United States to stabilize Venezuela”. Hegseth claimed US and Venezuelan armed forces would work together to attack “narco-terrorists” operating on Venezuelan soil, vowing: “We will hunt you down. We will find you. And we will kill you.”.

    Concluding her speech at the palace, Rodríguez told her foe-turned-friend: “Thank you, secretary, and I wish you a lifetime of happiness.”.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This is a roundup of the top stories from and about Germany on the weekend of Saturday, November 21, and Sunday, November 22, 2026:.
    • Harry Kane, Bayern Munich's star striker, has pledged to return to the field for the important matches at the end of the current campaign after undergoing surgery for a torn ankle ligament.
    • "I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season," he wrote on social media above a photo of himself on his hospital bed, also thanking fans for their messages of support.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This is a roundup of the top stories from and about Germany on the weekend of Saturday, November 21, and Sunday, November 22, 2026:.

    Harry Kane, Bayern Munich's star striker, has pledged to return to the field for the important matches at the end of the current campaign after undergoing surgery for a torn ankle ligament.

    "I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season," he wrote on social media above a photo of himself on his hospital bed, also thanking fans for their messages of support.

    Kane, 33, was injured around 20 minutes into Bayern's 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday.

    Bayern issued a statement on Saturday saying that Kane had "successfully undergone surgery" on his left ankle but was expected to be out for three to four months.

    England captain Kane, who finished the 2025–26 season with over 70 goals for club and country, was awarded the Ballon d'Or for his efforts.

    Hubert Aiwanger, the deputy premier and economy minister of the southern state of Bavaria, is being buried on Saturday in his native town of Inkofen.

    Aiwanger, the federal leader of the Free Voters (FW) party, died suddenly two weeks ago of natural causes at the age of 55 in a hotel in Berlin.

    The funeral service ahead of the burial was open to the public, with police saying they expected some 1,000 participants.

    A memorial service was held in Munich a week ago to honor Aiwanger.

    An online portal set up to collate records of right-wing violence in Germany since World War II is to lose its funding from the start of next year, a parliamentary inquiry has revealed.

    In response to a question from Green politician Marlene Schönberger, the minister of state for culture, Wolfram Weimer, remarked that "[a]dditional funds for financing beyond the end of 2026 are not available" for the online hub, hosted on the "Archivportal-D" of the German Digital Library.

    Schönberger, a member of the Bundestag's Committee on Internal Affairs, remarked she could not understand the decision by the government to cease funding for the portal.

    Recent findings suggest that "Not even eight months after the launch of the 'Right-Wing Violence' thematic portal, the federal government is now pulling the plug. That is completely incomprehensible," she stated.

    According to recent reports, "The federal government must prevent right-wing violence, and where it fails to do so, it must at least acknowledge and document its continuity. It owes that to those affected," she said.

    The hub was set up to bring together documents held in various archives in one online location.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    A judge in the US state of Missouri has approved a settlement under which Germany-based agrochemical company Bayer will pay up to $7.25 billion (€6.6 billion) over the next two decades to resolve lawsuits from cancer sufferers who say they should have been warned that its weed killer Roundup could cause lymphoma.

    The settlement, which applies nationwide, means both Roundup users who are already ill with non-Hodgkin lymphoma and those who develop it in future could an average of between $10,000 and $165,000, with factors such as their use of the product, their age at the time of diagnosis and illness severity determining the exact sum.

    The decision could be appealed.

    For more on this story, head over to our report.

    Young people in Germany, as in many other parts of the world, have been taking to the streets to demonstrate for a fairer, safer world and a greater say in what policies are enacted by politicians.

    But despite the fact that many of their complaints are fully justified, with jobs difficult to find despite a high level of study or training, housing that is increasingly unaffordable and a lack of government action against climate change to ensure the world remains habitable, the demonstrations have sometimes been criticized or even labeled as criminal.

    DW looks at the problems facing Gen Z and its fears about its future in a world where young people have little say.

    Many consumers who get their gas and electricity under the standard tariff offered by local utility providers will be paying considerably more for electricity and gas next year, according to comparison website Verivox.

    Some 3.7 million households are expected to pay more for electricity, with a rise of some 2% expected.

    The rise has been cushioned to some extent by coalition's recent agreement to lower the electricity tax rate for 2027 to the European minimum level to protect households and businesses.

    Gas will become considerably more expensive for some 1.9 million households, with 361 regional utility providers announcing rises of some 14% for December, January and February.

    "The wholesale prices for gas and electricity, which have risen sharply since the Iran war began in March 2026, are only now starting to have an effect on prices for consumers," Verivox energy expert Thorsten Storck said.

    Some 49% of people in Germany would like to see Berlin's financial, military and humanitarian aid to Ukraine amid the Russian invasion either reduced or cut completely, a survey has shown.

    In all, 25% of respondents in a YouGov survey wanted aid to Ukraine to be dropped, while 24% were in favor of reducing.

    Industry observers note that altogether 30% wanted to retain aid at the current level, and 9% felt it should be raised. Eleven percent were undecided on the issue.

    The survey was conducted between November 13 and 16 on behalf of the newspaper Welt am Sonntag.

    This week, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz hosted a meeting of Ukraine's European allies, known as the "Coalition of the Willing", in a bid to maintain a united front as peace talks in Ukraine continue.

    Guten Tag from DW's newsroom in Bonn!

    You join us as a survey highlights that support for Berlin's help to Kyiv amid the Russian invasion is declinin.

    And millions of households will see their electricity and gas bills rise considerably next year amid a number of geopolitical pressures.

    Read on for more on these and other stories hitting the headlines in Germany this weekend.

    #70333. Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1051 w)

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1051 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them.
    • Sources indicate that the exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does.
    • Industry observers note that to test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of Amazon Web Services access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.

    Sources indicate that the exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end consumers and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another major provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model.

    Industry observers note that to test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of Amazon Web Services access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible.

    In a recent development, the findings are striking. They included:.

    “We sent nearly two million AI prompts containing unique, trackable secrets to AI providers, then watched where those secrets surfaced,” Moore, the chief research officer of security firm Dragos, wrote Thursday. “What we found revealed security breaches, prompt theft, and widespread failures to protect customer data.”.

    According to recent reports, although prompts are encrypted in transit, they are decrypted at each hop inside the large inference reseller network. The prompt is first sent to an AI router, which reads the plaintext in it to determine the most suitable inference providers to handle the request. Often, the prompt is then sent to a pool of available models, which sometimes run inside different hosting providers. Prompts can also pass from one AI router (such as Vercel) to another one (e.g., OpenRouter). Each one of these players is likely to log the prompt and store it for as long as its policies call for (if not indefinitely).

    Sources indicate that the most concerning finding was the breach of three separate hosting providers. The attackers who compromised one of the providers reused “a couple hundred” of the AWS keys. Moore wrote:.

    It has been revealed that each key was sent in exactly one request to one provider, all within a few short windows in late October, and every request we sent during those windows was stolen. Some of the stolen keys came from requests that the provider rejected before a model ever ran—this tells us that the attacker was copying requests at the provider’s front door, and not somewhere deeper in the inference stack. In the other two breaches, some of the stolen requests were marked as ZDR. A privacy flag doesn’t help when the attacker is already inside.

    Industry observers note that parties tied to the hack of these three providers then tested each key, in some cases within hours of being seeded, to see what kind of resources it gave access to. The parties looked through S3 buckets, secrets managers, and parameter stores in search of still more credentials. They also tried to enable hosted models in AWS Bedrock and added their own IAM customers to maintain access. In all, the stolen bait keys were used “tens of thousands” of times in AWS API calls.

    Sources indicate that secrets sent to two of the hacked providers were swiftly used together, almost immediately, from the same rented server. That means the providers were almost certainly compromised by the same adversary.

    As noted earlier, some of the secrets were stolen by the resellers themselves. To lure prompts to their servers, they offered low prices. Then they turned on request logging and waited. Moore identified them by sending requests to the same model through different sellers. When credentials were later reused when sent through one seller and not another, the researcher knew it was the reseller, not the model provider, that was responsible.

    Sources indicate that last, the canary experiment revealed that some providers are scraping secret URLs put into the prompts, in violation of privacy terms. Moore wrote:.

    The clearest example involves a Chinese AI lab. This lab’s systems fetched the secret URLs from more than half of the prompts that we sent to its models between July and October, including roughly two-thirds of the requests marked as “no data collection” or Zero Data Retention. The scraper typically showed up two or three days after the request.

    Sources indicate that this wasn’t limited to requests sent to the lab directly. Several US hosting providers resell this lab’s models, and prompts sent to those providers triggered the exact same scraper—the prompts were flowing back to the lab. A customer who picked a US provider specifically to keep their data in the U.S. didn’t get what they paid for. Later on, a git client on a different cloud started trying to clone the private repositories referenced in our prompts, but only for prompts that used this lab’s models.

    The researcher stated he found one US hosting provider crawling a secret URL more than two months after it was used in a single inference call to its search endpoint. Another ran a scraper that came back for URLs days after each request, regardless of the AI router used to reach it.

    The blockbuster research is the latest indictment exposing the lax privacy and security that’s endemic in much of the AI ecosystem. The findings mean that people who want to ensure secrets they put into prompts stay private face a daunting task that isn’t likely to become easier any time soon.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse.
    • A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse.
    • It has been revealed that christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse.

    A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse.

    It has been revealed that christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami. He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States.

    He faces up to life in prison at sentencing.

    According to recent reports, federal prosecutors mentioned south Florida was a hub for planning and financing the plot to oust Moïse and install a president of the conspirators’ choosing. The government said Sanon was the conspirators’ initial choice for Moïse’s replacement. Prosecutors also said Sanon helped raise money for the conspiracy and arranged travel to Haiti and lodging for himself and others in that country.

    In a recent development, sanon acknowledged in trial testimony that he was in communication at one point with people trying to replace Moïse, but pointed out that the group had moved on to another candidate long before the assassination. He denied any knowledge of plans to kill Moïse.

    It has been revealed that sanon was born in Haiti and moved to the US as a teenager. He testified that he worked with churches in Haitian immigrant communities in Florida and the midwest.

    Sources indicate that haiti has not had a president since authorities said that a squad of mostly retired Colombian soldiers killed Moïse and wounded his wife in a night-time raid at their home on 7 July 2021. The poorest country in the Americas, Haiti has a history of dictatorship, political upheaval and foreign intervention that has long hindered democratic rule.

    The election of a fresh president is scheduled for next year.

    Prosecutors said the scheme to kill Moïse included paying about two dozen foreign mercenaries with money obtained from US government programs that were intended to help businesses during the Covid pandemic, according to court records. US prosecutors have charged more than 40 people with crimes related to the assassination and a dozen have been convicted, including five who are serving life sentences.

    According to recent reports, the plot to oust Moïse began taking final shape in April 2021, when Sanon met in south Florida with a former Haitian senator and several US businesspeople, according to an indictment. The group agreed that Sanon, once in power, would award contracts to two Florida-based companies – Counter Terrorist Unit Federal Academy and Counter Terrorist Unit Security, collectively known as CTU – for infrastructure projects, security forces and military equipment, according to investigators.

    CTU initially hired about 18 Colombian nationals with military training to provide security for Sanon, according to prosecutors. Conspirators also spent months obtaining weapons and body armor and attempting to build ties with Haitian gangs, officials said.

    Recent findings suggest that by June 2021, the conspirators realized Sanon had neither the constitutional qualifications nor sufficient popular support to become president. They shifted their support to Wendelle Coq Thélot, a former Haitian supreme court judge who died in January 2025 while a fugitive.

    Sanon was previously scheduled to be tried with four other men who were convicted earlier this year, but his case was separated from theirs and delayed for health reasons.

    • Recent findings suggest that california’s Attorney General Rob Bonta on Thursday evening said the state has served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia following news of former CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman who the U.S.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that california’s Attorney General Rob Bonta on Thursday evening said the state has served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia following news of former CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman who the U.S. government believes is a Chinese spy.

    The state is investigating the company to find out if its advanced GPUs or confidential information may have been shared with China, and if the company had somehow misled its investors and the public.

    “The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the manufacturer may have misled investors,” Bonta said in a statement.

    “My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang’s actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information — and if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law,” he added.

    The investigation comes in the wake of a messy couple of weeks for Nvidia, which has overnight come under intense scrutiny around the world due to the implications of Huang’s alleged relationship with the Chinese national, Alice Huang (who is not related to Jensen).

    The Nvidia founder resigned last week after further revelations of extramarital affairs with the company’s employees. And while many tech voices have been petitioning Nvidia to bring back Huang as CEO, saying they see him as indispensable to the further development of the AI industry, the company’s new chair, Harvey Jones, remarked earlier this week that Nvidia had no intention of reinstating Huang to his position.

    The tech giant’s board has hired a law firm as well as an independent slate of directors to investigate the extent of the damage, and the U.S. government is trying to find out the extent of Alice Huang’s ties with the Chinese government.

    It has been revealed that the U.S. Congress is also gearing up to subpoena Huang, seeking questions about the affair, and the SEC is said to be launching a civil probe into the company, trying to find out if Nvidia’s public disclosures could have misled investors.

    Industry observers note that democratic representatives have also opened an inquiry into the Trump administration’s management of Nvidia’s chip sales to China. In a scathing letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Democrats last week asked the Commerce Department to preserve records about an arrangement that they called questionable and illegal.

    “Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: Companies cannot mislead their investors,” Bonta wrote.

    Huang has agreed to testify before Congress after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him.

    Mamdani introduces blueprint to close Upcoming York's Rikers Island jail by 2032

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Perched on a 413 acre (167 hectare) island between Queens and the Bronx, the notorious Rikers Island jail complex earned a variety of nicknames over the years.
    • Fresh York City's official overseeing the closure of the city's most notorious jail hopes a new plan from Mayor Zohran Mamdani will lead to "a moment of transformation" for how people are detained in the largest US city.
    • Mamdani on Friday unveiled a blueprint to close the Rikers Island complex by 2032, to build four latest jails and drastically reduce the city's detainee population.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Perched on a 413 acre (167 hectare) island between Queens and the Bronx, the notorious Rikers Island jail complex earned a variety of nicknames over the years.

    Fresh York City's official overseeing the closure of the city's most notorious jail hopes a new plan from Mayor Zohran Mamdani will lead to "a moment of transformation" for how people are detained in the largest US city.

    Mamdani on Friday unveiled a blueprint to close the Rikers Island complex by 2032, to build four latest jails and drastically reduce the city's detainee population.

    Intends to shutter the troubled facility date back to 2019, when the city council first voted to close it by this year. But plans have been delayed over the years in part due to the logistical difficulties over where to place inmates.

    Dana Kaplan - who Mamdani appointed as the city's "Close Rikers Czar" told the BBC News channel on Friday that his latest proposal is not just about getting rid of a decrepit facility.

    It is also a "generational opportunity" to "build a different type of detention system" and figure out how to detain people more appropriately, she said.

    Sources indicate that the Rikers Island jail complex is perched on a 413 acre (167 hectare) island between Queens and the Bronx, and has earned a variety of nicknames over the years because of its dilapidated conditions, including Gladiator School and Torture Island. The jail has housed a number of high-profile inmates awaiting trial, including Tupac Shakur, DMX and Harvey Weinstein.

    It houses more than 6,500 inmates at a given time. Mamdani hopes to reduce that number to 4,100 - a goal that has been met with skepticism by the Latest York City correction officers' union.

    Recent findings suggest that "[B]uilding a new system that puts an arbitrary cap on the City's available jail beds is ill-conceived, irresponsible and jeopardizes the safety of all New Yorkers, including our Officers," NYC Correction Officers' Benevolent Association said in a statement. "The City cannot keep the jail population at around 4,100 without irresponsibly releasing individuals who committed violent felony charges.".

    "It's actually possible to have fewer people in jail in New York City - and that is what we should be planning for," she mentioned.

    It has been revealed that the jail complex has long faced backlash over staffing shortages, crumbling conditions and inmate deaths in the facility, including nine this year. Legislation required the jail to be shuttered by 2027, but Mamdani blamed lags under former Mayor Eric Adams' administration as well as the Covid pandemic for the delays.

    Last year, under Adams, a federal judge removed Rikers from the city's control, appointing an independent outside official to make decisions concerning the facility.

    In an 88-page report released on Friday, Mamdani mentioned Rikers was a product of "deteriorating infrastructure" and that officials had a "moral imperative" to close it.

    New York City Council must approve the updated timeline, with members, including the city's speaker, indicating they support the initiative.

    Mamdani's office mentioned the city would open up four new jails - one in Brooklyn by 2029, two in the Bronx and Queens by 2031 and one in Manhattan by 2032.

    In a recent development, the mayor's office argues the new, smaller facilities will provide inmates "access to daylight, fresh air and clean space" leading to better outcomes for detainees. The facilities will be easier for families to access as well, as travel to the remote Rikers can take hours.

    Mamdani noted his administration would work to reduce the number of people being held in jail across Newly introduced York City, including by offering alternative programmes to detention for some awaiting trial, by making it easier for families to post bail online and by trying to speed up the pretrial legal process.

    He also wants to open up hundreds of beds in therapeutic housing units for prisoners with serious mental health challenges.

    Kaplan stated Mamdani's administration had already opened 100 therapeutic beds at Bellevue Hospital in Manhattan, moving 100 people off of Rikers Island.

    The proposal involves a large investments: $146m (Â£111m) for mental health and substance use treatment and vocational and education programming inside and outside the jails.

    Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (693 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Meta’s executives are rethinking the manufacturer’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030.
    • The manufacturer’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta.
    • “We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Meta’s executives are rethinking the manufacturer’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030. That revelation in Meta’s latest sustainability report comes as the company reported a record percentage increase in greenhouse gas emissions that exceeds any other Big Tech competitor racing to build fresh AI data centers.

    The manufacturer’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta. In the November 19, 2026, report, they attributed the changing conditions and the need for a rethink to how “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.”.

    “We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report.

    Meta’s statement about re-evaluating its 2030 emissions goal is a significant public acknowledgment, given that Amazon, Google, and Microsoft have all stuck by their original sustainability goals so far.

    Industry observers note that but all the companies have acknowledged challenges in balancing their original sustainability goals against the breakneck buildout of hyperscale data centers. Despite efforts to invest in more renewable energy projects, Meta and its rivals are still often pushing forward on AI data centers that rely on burning natural gas to generate electricity.

    Meta’s report described the manufacturer’s total emissions as surging from 15.6 million metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2024 to more than 21.7 million metric tonnes in 2025.

    According to recent reports, that would make Meta’s annual carbon footprint roughly comparable to total emissions for the state of Idaho, while surpassing the total emissions of states such as Hawaii, Maine, South Dakota, and Upcoming Hampshire. The firm attributed much of this emissions increase to “capital goods,” like as data center servers.

    That also represents a nearly 40 percent increase in Meta’s carbon footprint between 2024 and 2025, which is the highest percentage year-over-year increase for total emissions reported by any of the four major US tech giants.

    For comparison, Microsoft reported a 25 percent increase in its overall carbon footprint, Google reported an 18 percent increase, and Amazon’s report described a 16 percent increase between 2024 and 2025. However, Meta still likely has one of the smallest total carbon footprints among the Major Tech companies.

    Meta’s approach to achieving net-zero emissions has included developing upcoming renewable energy projects to match emissions and using carbon removal technology.

    Industry observers note that but even when factoring in such efforts, Meta still reported net emissions increasing from more than 8.1 million metric tonnes to more than 11.8 million metric tonnes for 2025. That represents a 45 percent increase.

    From a water consumption standpoint, Meta reported progress in reducing facility consumption from 825 million gallons in 2024 to 790 million gallons in 2025.

    Yet that positive trend is tempered by the fact that Meta also described an increase in water consumption from “areas with water stress,” rising from 198 million gallons in 2024 to 246 million gallons in 2025.

    Meta also reported a sharp increase in water consumption related to purchased electricity—the amount of water consumed by related power generation—from 19 billion gallons in 2024 to more than 26 billion gallons in 2025. This once again highlights that, for data centers, the far bigger water usage comes from the power plants that supply electricity to data centers as opposed to data centers directly using water for cooling.

    Sources indicate that still, some minor credit is due. The publication Data Center Dynamics pointed out that “Meta is the only hyperscaler to report indirect water use, a growing concern as data centers shift to closed-loop cooling systems that, despite using less water at source, require more electricity to run.”.

    It would very much be in the public interest for other Massive Tech companies to follow suit on the reporting front—and public pressure continues to build after the AI backlash impact on US midterm election results.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A mathematician working for AI giant Anthropic indicates he used the company's Claude AI tool to solve one of mathematics most famous problems.
    • The Riemann hypothesis dates back to 1859 and centers on the distribution of prime numbers underpinning a much wider scope of mathematical work.
    • Levent Alpoge, a member of Anthropic's technical staff, made the announcement on his website.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A mathematician working for AI giant Anthropic indicates he used the company's Claude AI tool to solve one of mathematics most famous problems.

    The Riemann hypothesis dates back to 1859 and centers on the distribution of prime numbers underpinning a much wider scope of mathematical work.

    Levent Alpoge, a member of Anthropic's technical staff, made the announcement on his website. "I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis," Levent Alpoge wrote in a note released Friday.

    Sources indicate that the proof still has to be verified and confirmed by other mathematicians. If it withstands independent examination, it would be a major milestone both in mathematics and the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI) in scientific research.

    The Riemann hypothesis is the latest and most key in a string of famous mathematical problems that were tackled with the help of AI.

    Alpoge mentioned that the collaboration with AI had generated more than 250,000 pages of mathematical material, adding that he had not yet mastered all the mathematics involved.

    Sources indicate that "Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line," he wrote. "No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.".

    The Riemann Hypothesis is one of seven major mathematical problems, the so-called Millennium Prize Problems, selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which offers $1 million for a solution to each of those.

    "This is an announcement of historic significance," Martin Bridson, president of the institute, said in a statement quoted by news agency AP.

    He added it "holds the promise of a dramatic transformation in the perception of what is possible in the struggle to extend the human understanding of mathematics.".

    "But the journey from today’s announcement to a place of real understanding will be long and difficult.".

    Formulated by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in the 19th century, the hypothesis is about the distribution of prime numbers, which are numbers that can only be divided by themselves and the number 1.

    The hypothesis describes a fundamental pattern of how these numbers are distributed as they become ever larger. Confirming that hypothesis is thought to have crucial implications for a wide range of further mathematical research.

    The potential breakthrough by Alpoge and Claude AI comes amid a growing number of examples where artificial intelligence systems are making significant contributions to advanced mathematical research.

    In September, rival AI company OpenAI said its technology had helped solve a problem involving the Navier-Stokes equations.

    The equations, which describe the movement of fluids such as water and air, are another of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, but the claim that they've been solved also still needs independent verification.

    It has been revealed that google is announcing some significant changes to its smart home software. Starting next year, the company will shut down the Nest app in favor of the Google Home app and retire Google Assistant on its smart home devices.

    In a recent development, the Nest app shutdown takes place on January 25th, 2027, meaning you’ll have to manage your Nest products, including Nest thermostats, cameras, and Nest Protect alarms, from the Google Home app instead.     The changes for Google Assistant will take place later: On August 2nd, 2027, the Gemini for Home voice assistant will replace Google Assistant on smart speakers and smart displays, the company says. Google argues that Gemini for Home allows users to ask more complex questions and speak naturally instead of needing to use dedicated commands or specific language.

    According to recent reports, gemini for Home was announced last year, so it’s not exactly a shock that Google is going to move on from Google Assistant in the smart home (especially when the organization also killed Google Assistant on phones earlier this year).     💡 Key Takeaways
    • Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner.
    • The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers.
    • Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner.

    The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations.

    Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.

    Despite countries not being required to reveal how they voted, it is thought Grynspan’s candidature has been resisted by Russia and the US, two of the five permanent security council members that can ultimately wield a veto against a candidate. Knowledge among the security council delegations of how countries are voting is down to private intelligence, leaks and a process of elimination.

    The intensive lobbying over the job has spread across the globe, but Friday is especially key since the poll is slated to differentiate the voting of the P5 from the 10 elected members (E10) of the security council. To be recommended as secretary general to the UN general assembly, a candidate needs nine votes and no vetoes. In Friday’s colour-coded secret ballot, the P5 will cast red ballots and the E10 white.

    One diplomat said: “The electoral system means it is important how many votes you win, but equally how many of certain votes you don’t lose.”.

    The protracted 140-day deadlock confirms the polarisation that has hampered the incumbent secretary general, António Guterres, but also belies claims the role is now an irrelevance.

    Friday’s secret ballot may also reveal whether the United Arab Emirates’ campaign for its diplomat, Lana Nusseibeh, is about to blow up in its face due to the hostility to the UAE’s brand of active, commercially driven diplomacy, not just in Sudan, but also Somalia, Western Sahara, Libya and Yemen.

    A late entrant, in the two straw polls in which she has contested so far, Nusseibeh secured only seven “encourage” votes, six “discourage” and two “no opinions”. This is despite prestigious significant-power backing and her acknowledged personal diplomatic skills.

    According to recent reports, nusseibeh has US and Russian backing. The French foreign ministry may have misgivings about the UAE, but Emmanuel Macron, the French president, travelled to the UAE in the midst of French riots to see the UAE president, Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, and secure 100,000 metric tons of diesel a month.

    Recent findings suggest that in the UK, the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, has kept his counsel, but he shares a Polish-Jewish refugee heritage with Grynspan and cannot be an admirer of the UAE’s human rights record or its evasion of EU sanctions on Russia. The prime minister, Andy Burnham, has UAE connections from his time as mayor of Manchester, and Nusseibeh is a fellow alumnus of the University of Cambridge. At the UN she worked closely with the UK in an informal group called “Friends of the Future of the UN”.

    Yet 68 British MPs, including the Labour chair of the international development select committee, Sarah Champion, last week signed a letter calling on Burnham to veto Nusseibeh, describing her as “a tainted and compromised figure”.

    Some of the opposition to her from elected security council members is not wholly political. Latin American countries believe an informal rotation system means it is their turn to lead the UN. As a result Panama and Colombia, right now on the security council, will oppose her. China has also been supportive of this rotation principle.

    Recent findings suggest that but others deeply object to what they consider to be the UAE’s dollar diplomacy and preparedness to use its extraordinary wealth to exacerbate and exploit pre-existing divisions in a country to gain a commercial foothold. Somalia, for instance, has a seat on the Security Council, and its president, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, this week went on TV to accuse the UAE of buying ports, establishing military bases and supporting armed forces outside Somalia’s national security framework without federal approval.

    It is also possible that Finland and Latvia, the two elected members with the greatest stake in Ukraine, are unimpressed that the UAE gave Vladimir Putin red carpet treatment when he visited Abu Dhabi in December 2023, nine months after the international criminal court had issued an arrest warrant for child trafficking. Greece, less engaged in Ukraine, may be more flexible.

    Industry observers note that since the last poll, Nusseibeh has been to Bahrain, Britain and Pakistan, a clue as to where extra votes may be harvested. She also had a “thoughtful exchange” with Zeng Jixin, the Chinese ambassador to the UAE.

    Industry observers note that the two hurdles are whether someone so deep inside the UAE inner circle would have the courage in office to show true independence, and whether her active denials of UAE involvement in arming the RSF in Sudan leave her irretrievably tainted. From a Palestinian intellectual family, she insists she would make peace in Sudan her number one priority.

    In the last ballot on 5 November, Grynspan won 12 votes in favour and three negative. But on 16 October – the only colour-coded ballot so far – which distinguishes between permanent and elected members – she received two discourage votes from permanent members, the equivalent of a veto. Nusseibeh had not joined the race at that point.

    In an administration as personalised as the US, it has been hard for Grynspan to gain influence, with many sensing that Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the UN, is the key influencer.

    It has been revealed that grynspan has been reluctant to make the fact she is Jewish a feature of her candidacy, but the election of a Jewish person to run the UN might be seen as something the US could embrace as transformative. Her age – she is 70 – could be considered a drawback among those calling for a younger generation to renew the institution.

    Although there are other Latin American candidates, Grynspan is seen as a more viable candidate than her rival, the Argentine Rafael Grossi, the head of the UN weapons inspectorate. Russia has opposed Grossi, objecting to his interventions over the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant in Ukraine.

    One way or the other, the logjam has to be broken soon.

    Levent AlpÃ¶ge mentioned, external on Friday, a day after Anthropic made its US stock market debut, that over the course of about six weeks, he used the Claude chatbot to create a detailed proof of the maths problem.

    Sources indicate that if found to be correct, the proof would be among the most significant in history. AlpÃ¶ge described it as "one dawn across science of something far greater".

    The claim comes as AI firms like OpenAI have in recent months announced scores of solutions to major higher maths problems that have eluded scholars for decades.

    As for the Riemann hypothesis proof put forward on Friday, it was found using a non-public version of Anthropic's Claude.

    It is a nearly 170-year-old maths problem that deals with prime numbers and is widely considered to be the single most famous problem in maths, in large part due to how complex it is.

    Named after the mathematician Bernhard Riemann, the hypothesis puts forward that prime numbers have a determined order along the number line.

    Prime numbers are the bedrock of higher maths, leaving breakthroughs related to them to have broad impact.

    AlpÃ¶ge remarked that he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Sunday, asking him directly about how he could announce the discovery.

    "The precise timing is horrible," AlpÃ¶ge mentioned, referring to Anthropic's public stock listing. "If I could have, I'd have finished this all much earlier.".

    The complete textual proof that AlpÃ¶ge put forward in Lean, a computer language used for confirming maths proofs, is over 250,000 pages long.
